frozen_original.title: FBI Under Kash Patel Opens Investigations of Journalists Who Covered Trump Negatively
frozen_original.synopsis: In February 2025, reports emerged that the FBI under Director Kash Patel had opened leak investigations targeting journalists and news organizations that had published critical coverage of Trump, including reporters at major outlets who had covered the Russia investigation, January 6, and Trump's business dealings. frozen_original.title: Trump Ends Community Development Block Grant Program
frozen_original.synopsis: In March 2025, the Trump administration terminated the Community Development Block Grant program — a flexible federal funding stream that had for 50 years provided cities and counties with resources to fund affordable housing, infrastructure improvements, economic development, and social services in low-income communities. CDBG grants totaling approximately $3.3 billion annually had funded everything from senior center repairs to small business development to community health clinics in thousands of communities across all 50 states. The termination left local governments scrambling to fill funding gaps for programs that had no alternative federal funding source. Mayors from both parties condemned the elimination. Housing advocates warned the loss of CDBG would accelerate urban disinvestment and worsen affordable housing shortages in already distressed communities.

merged_description_snapshot.description_long: On August 18, 2026, The New Republic reported that the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency had conditionally approved World Liberty Financial’s application to create a national trust bank, to be called World Liberty Trust Company. The article said the Trump family owned a 38% stake in World Liberty Financial and received 75% of its crypto revenue. It also reported that Donald Trump had collected nearly $600 million from the company in the prior year, citing his financial disclosure. The conditional approval followed a broader increase in applications for national bank charters under the Trump administration; the article said final approval still depended on the company raising sufficient capital. The author argued the arrangement raised a conflict because the president’s family could benefit financially from a company receiving federal banking approval under an administration led by Trump. The article was an opinion piece criticizing the decision and describing it as self-dealing. Conditional approval was not the same as a final charter, and the report did not describe a legal finding that officials had violated banking law or improperly influenced the application.
merged_description_snapshot.description_medium: A New Republic opinion article reported that the Trump family’s crypto company, World Liberty Financial, received conditional approval for a national trust bank charter in August 2026. The article said the family owned 38% of the company and received 75% of its crypto revenue. The approval was conditional, not a final charter or proof of unlawful conduct.
merged_description_snapshot.notes: The New Republic article is an opinion piece. It reports conditional OCC approval and family ownership/revenue figures, while arguing that the approval raises conflict-of-interest concerns. The approval was not final and the article reports no legal finding of wrongdoing.
